newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JANZEN CHARGES INTO THREE-SHOT LEAD AT PGA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JANZEN CHARGES INTO THREE-SHOT LEAD AT PGA.

text.p: Lee Janzen picked up where he left off on Thursday, unleashing a spectacular birdie binge at Winged Foot to seize a three-stroke lead late in the second round of the PGA Championship.

Janzen, who had six birdies on the back nine in his opening- round 71, posted five birdies in his first 10 holes Friday to charge past a faltering John Daly and put some distance between himself and a crowded group on the leaderboard.
The 1993 U.S. Open champion stood at six-under par, with Tom Kite, Davis Love, Fred Couples and Justin Leonard his closest pursuers at three-under.
Daly, who thrilled the fans and his fellow-players alike with a record-tying opening round of 66 as he continues his comeback from alcoholism, held the lead until his 12th hole.
Daly went on to bogey four more holes after he was overtaken to finish the day with a three-over-par 73 for a one-under total of 139.

"I just missed a lot of putts. I missed a lot of four or five-footers," said Daly, who missed the Masters and British Open after undergoing alcoholism treatment, and walked off the course at the U.S. Open in the second round with a case of the shakes.
"If someone told me I'd be one-under after two days I'd have taken it," said Daly.
"Any time you're three or four shots out in the last two rounds of a major you have a chance."
Daly and Love dueled for the lead in the beginning of the round, and then it became a free for all until Janzen took charge.

Tiger Woods looked set to make a big charge as he birdied his first two holes after a level-par opening round, but the 21-year-old Masters champion had putting problems that slowed his momentum and he stood at one under through 15.

British Open champion Justin Leonard briefly joined a three-way tie for the lead with Daly and Tom Kite at four under but he fell back bogeys at the eighth and 10th before getting back on track with a birdie at 12.
Kite was alone in the lead until he bogyed the ninth hole to fall back to three under.
Couples holed out from the fairway at the par-4 11th hole for eagle and added two more birdies to climb to four under before a bogey at the 16th.
Love was the leader in the clubhouse at three-under 137 after a roller-coaster round that included four birdies, three bogeys and a double bogey for a 71.

A group of five players were in the clubhouse at two-under- par 138 including Italian Costantino Rocca, who birdied the last two holes for his second successive 69, and Phil Mickelson, who used an eagle at the par-5 12th hole to post his second 69.
Another shot back were Greg Norman and Paul Stankowski.
